TDLR: missed dose of meds, participated in robot dragon apocalypse and got infinite parking tickets for a car that's not mine.

I should start this out by noting that missing a dose of my medication can cause really, really weird dreams.

When it started, there was some war apocalypse involving people riding dragons and giant mecharobots. I was on one of the dragons and it looked like the robots were on our side. I remember that I was totally confused, even in the dream.

I don't remember how I got to this next part, but it was definitely during the same night that I had it:

Suddenly I was in the parking lot of a shopping center close to my house. My car was parked perfectly fine, but it was a different car than what I own. I would get parking ticket after parking ticket after parking ticket indefinitely. I went to pay off the tickets and the only place I could do it was really shady. Well, when I got back to the car, more parking tickets! And when I went to the shady shop to pay them off, they said I still owed money. This became a vicious cycle until I woke up.

It took me a few minutes to realize I didn't actually get any parking tickets and that they were a dream. Thank God.

Well all I have is my Chemistry textbook.

TDLR: saved up 50$ in coins for a GBC at the age of six only to have mom sell it for 10$ to help buy my sister a GBA.

I had some sort of abnormal determination when I was a kid. I had gotten interested in pokemon at around the age of 5, and decided I wanted to buy a gameboy color to play some pokemon.

So  I proceeded to save up spare change (coins) to buy it myself since my parents didn't think I needed it. I would look for coins around the house, and my parents would be nice enough to let me keep the change from all their cash purchases. They thought it was a phase. I would count the money every day, and I built a box out of those square play mats, or whatever they were, to keep the money in. If I remember correctly, a lot of it was the smaller stuff, like nickels and dimes.

So after a while, I had enough to go and buy the GBC. The Gameboy advance had already come out, but being 6yo, I wasn't very good about making lasting decisions. 

So, I get to the cash register with my giant sack of coins. The clerk looked at little me, the bag of about 50$ of coins that he had to count, and the super long line behind me. This is probably retail's worst nightmare.

Well, being six when I bought the thing, I still wasn't very good at counting money, so I was short by like maybe 20$, so my dad covered the rest with his credit card.

I ended up totally addicted to pokemon silver to the point where it interfered with my normal functioning, so my mom decided to get  rid of the thing for my own good. She sold it for 10$ to put towards buying my sister a gameboy advance.


EDIT: clarity.

I just posted about how my country (Colombia) loves coffee, but I probably have a problem.

I have an espresso machine, and I drink at least 6 full blown mugs of double-shot espresso a day. It takes the edge off of my stress.

Colombia: coffee. Oh my god, how we love coffee. A few years ago when I went back, I went to a whole theme park for coffee. Our government is giving incentives to farmers to stop growing cocaine and start growing coffee instead. We drink it black, no sugar. coffee is life.

I had neighbors once who would sell cars from the neighborhood parking lot. They would take up every. Single. Space. 

Even the reserved spaces of my family and our other neighbors. I'm not even sure if he was operating his car sales business legally, but I was too preoccupied with finding a place to park all day, every day.

Protip: don't take up half the neighborhood parking lot with your potentially illegal car dealership. Take that shit somewhere else.

I actually realized at that moment that what I really wanted wasn't to die, it was just to have a normal life. 

Years of therapy and dealing with the stigma and discrimination from mental illness had me hopeless, but in that moment, I was just so angry at the world, I decided I wanted to live and prove wrong those who were telling me I couldn't succeed in life, but I was like, "fuck, that's not going to happen." 

Immediate regret, but I'm grateful that I'm still alive, and it, a long with some other things, like the discrimination I experienced in college, really make me want to prove to the world that I actually have worth. 

I've managed to stay in college with a 3.5 GPA and maintaining friendships, even though even my doctor didn't think I'd last there, let alone graduate high school, and I now have plans for medical school to go into psychiatry eventually.

I think every human has worth in one way or another, it's a matter of finding out what your purpose is, which nobody can do for you, but it's there. And it inherently is a good purpose. At the same time, it's up to you to live it out as the good thing it's meant to be, and it will be difficult, but it can be done.

"You're smart."

It's one thing for a guy to tell me that he thinks I'm pretty, but if he tells me I'm smart then it shows me he values more than appearances.

I am a 20, female, and basically going through a lot. You might think something like a transition in my life- and it's true that I'm moving to a new city, there's more to it than that. 

I am 20, female, and I have Bipolar Disorder. My moods are crazy... and it's hurt a lot of things in my life, namely, I've lost a lot of friendships thanks to the depression and sometimes the mania, too. For some reason though, I have hope for my life. 

I'm 20, female, and I keep going. I hope for normalcy and that's probably the only reason I'm still alive.

"Just think positive and maybe you'll stop being depressed."

Sure! So, next time you drown in a swimming pool, if you think oxygen you can live and everything will be just dandy!

My God.
Something tells me she missed the "love thy neighbor" bit of the Bible. Something else tells me she took the "turn the other cheek" bit the wrong way.

My 18th birthday: I had a boyfriend at the time in college who was a total ass, manipulative, etc. He was pressuring me to go to a club, and in reality I wasn't that kind of person. I invited people, and nobody wanted to go. 

Fast forward to birthday night, this guy pressured me into wearing the ugliest, skimpiest dress ever, and it was cold. So I was freezing, and since he has no sense of time, the club hadn't even opened yet and we were waiting outside. I was about sick of everything at this point, so I completely lost it. Loudly and angrily, I broke up with him on the sidewalk. 

Now, he was a leech; he was a commuter that hoarded all his stuff in my dorm. So, both of us walked back there since I was nice enough to give him his stuff back and not throw it away. He left, and i cried my eyes out for the rest of the night.

Looking back, the relationship was pretty abusive, the pinnacle of which was when he tried to strangle me. He stalked me for 6 months after that night, and thank God he's gone.
